Settling unpaid taxes when you sell

Your title company asks the Treasury Bureau for the amount owed and pays it from your sale proceeds at closing, so a delinquent balance does not block a sale. The balance does reduce what you receive.

The city's online property information tool is updated nightly and should not be used for final billings or closings, because unbilled taxes, fines and fees may exist. Three separate calls cover the gaps: the Treasury Bureau for taxes, the Water Department at 585-428-5990 for water, and the Municipal Code Violations Bureau for fines and tickets. If the house has inherited or exemption history, mention that to the title company early so a supplemental tax does not surprise anyone.

For a sale where you want to skip repairs, that list is also your pre-listing checklist. A buyer paying cash for the house as it stands still needs a clean payoff letter, and getting it before the contract is signed shortens the closing.

Housing in Rochester

Rochester is a renter-heavy city, with 38.1 percent of homes owner-occupied. The July 2025 population estimate is 206,108, down 2.4 percent from the April 2020 base. Median value of owner-occupied homes is $139,600 and median gross rent is $1,081. Heavy lake effect snow, averaging just over 100 inches a year, is worth remembering when a buyer's inspector looks at roofs and gutters, and values on a Browncroft or Charlotte street can look very different from the citywide median.

Frequently asked questions

Do I owe Monroe County tax on a Rochester house?

Yes. Rochester properties get a Monroe County bill in addition to the city and school bill, and the county bill is issued on December 31. The city bill does not include county charges, so call the Monroe County Real Property Tax Service Office at 585-753-1125 for county balances.

Can I sell a Rochester house if I owe back taxes?

Yes. The unpaid amount, with interest at 1 percent per month on late installments, is paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasury Bureau for a current payoff before you accept an offer.

Is there a way to pay overdue Rochester taxes over time?

Yes. The Director of Finance can approve a delinquency or tax agreement for eligible owners, and a parcel under an active agreement is protected from lien sale. Call the Treasury Bureau at 585-428-6940 to ask whether you qualify.

Which Rochester exemption deadline is next?

February 1, 2027, a Monday. Exemption applications and renewals for seniors, military service and disabled owners must be at the Bureau of Assessment by then.

What is the deadline to challenge my Rochester assessment?

8 p.m. Eastern on the third Tuesday in March, which is March 16, 2027, with the form received at City Hall Room 101A. Missing it leaves informal review between July 1 and January 1 and a Small Claims Assessment Review filing by May 30.

Where to pay Schenectady property tax

City and county taxes go to the City of Schenectady Bureau of Receipts. School taxes go to the school district instead, and that has been the arrangement since 2007. Because the two bills are collected by different offices, a single payoff letter will not show everything you owe when you sell.

The city bill rolls city and county taxes together with water and sewer charges and, where it applies, the trash fee. The Bureau of Receipts works from City Hall, Room 100, 105 Jay Street, and its number is 518-382-5016. For school tax, call the district at 518-881-3988. The assessment office is a separate counter in the same building, Room 8.

Due dates and ways to pay

Bills are issued on January 1 of each year and are payable quarterly, in January, April, July and October. Most upstate bills arrive once or twice a year, so owners new to the city are sometimes surprised by the pace.

There are three ways to pay the city:

  • By mail to City of Schenectady, PO Box 947, Schenectady, New York 12301. Send a check with the detached stub, never cash, and tick the receipt box on the coupon if you want a receipt back.
  • In person through the drop box on Franklin Street. Use your own envelope for the stub and a check or money order. Anything left after hours is processed the next business day.

A payment without the stub is still accepted if the property address is written on it. If a closing is a few weeks away, ask the Bureau which quarters are still open so you know what the title company will collect.

Assessment calendar

Send the state grievance form, RP-524, to the City Assessor. You can mail it, email it to grievance@schenectadyny.gov, or drop it off at 105 Jay Street, Room 8. The assessment office phone is 518-382-5075.

  • Email applications should carry the property address and the SBL (tax map) number in the subject line, with the form attached as a PDF.
  • For mailed forms, include a self-addressed stamped envelope or an email address so the office can send back a receipt.
  • Hand-delivered forms get a photocopy of the first page as the receipt.
  • The board reads every application received during the period, even if you never appear in person, and skipping the hearing does not count against you.

The grievance route only works inside the window. A seller who misses it should price the house with the current assessment in mind and let buyers know the figure is open to challenge next spring.

What is on your assessment record?

The roll lists the property class, build year, condition, bedrooms, baths, fireplaces and square footage the assessor has on file. Check each item before a buyer does. A wrong bedroom count, or a missing note about a gutted kitchen, changes the value the city assigns.

Class codes read 210 for a single family house, 220 for two family, 230 for three family and 280 for a multiple residence. Land frontage and depth come from tax maps supplied by Schenectady County Real Property. If something on the card is wrong, call the assessment office at 518-382-5075 and ask how to correct it.

The state tax department publishes the downloadable exemption forms, and the city's assessment page links to guidance on contesting an assessment. What happens to unpaid taxes?

An unpaid balance stays attached to the parcel. The Bureau of Receipts is the office to ask for the exact amount and which quarters are open. Request the figure by phone or at the counter rather than estimating it.

New York sets a two-year redemption period for property under a delinquent tax lien, and a taxing district can lengthen it for homes. The rule is in RPTL section 1110.

Ask for a payoff in writing, and ask the school district for its own figure, since school taxes are collected separately.

Selling with taxes owed

The closing agent requests payoff amounts from the Bureau of Receipts and the school district and pays them out of the sale price. Owing tax does not stop a sale. It only lowers your net.

The city bill folds in water, sewer and the trash fee, so an old utility balance can sit inside what looks like a tax figure. Read the breakdown line by line. If a quarter has just come due, ask whether the closing agent will treat it as owed by you or prorate it with the buyer.

A short checklist helps the process move:

  • Find your latest city bill and the quarterly stubs you have already paid.
  • Check the assessment card for errors and note the Grievance Day date for the buyer.
  • List any exemption you hold, since the buyer must apply on their own.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and repair requests, so the open tax figure is usually the main item left to settle before the closing date.

Schenectady housing at a glance

About 45.6 percent of Schenectady homes are owner-occupied, and the 2025 population estimate is 69,471, up 3.6 percent from the April 2020 base. The city covers 10.79 square miles of land, with 29,184 households averaging 2.22 persons each.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020-2024: $168,800.
  • Median gross rent: $1,145.

Older houses are common here, and the Stockade Historic District and the General Electric Realty Plot beside Union College hold some of the oldest homes. Buyers of those houses ask about roofs, wiring and heating, so gather any receipts for recent work.

Four. Bills are issued January 1 and payable in January, April, July and October. School tax is a separate payment made to the school district.

Yes. The city runs an electronic bill pay site, and the Bureau of Receipts also takes mail payments and check or money order drops in the Franklin Street box.

When is Schenectady Grievance Day?

The fourth Tuesday in May, with the grievance period opening May 1. In 2027 that falls on May 25.

Who do I call about a Schenectady exemption?

Call the assessment office at 518-382-5075 or visit City Hall, Room 8. Exemption applications are due by the March 1 taxable status date.

No. The city bill covers city and county taxes plus water, sewer and the trash fee where it applies, and school tax is paid to the district. Ask both offices for payoff figures before you close.

Who collects Smithtown property tax and who sets the amount

The Town of Smithtown Receiver of Taxes collects the whole bill: town, Suffolk County and school district levies together. The receiver sets no rate. The Department of Assessment values each parcel, and the elected boards of the school districts, county, town, villages and fire districts decide how much money they need.

Think of the levy as a pie. The levy is the whole pie, and your assessment only decides how big a slice you carry. For most households the school district portion is the largest part of the bill, and it follows the budget residents vote on each May.

Smithtown had an estimated 116,847 residents in July 2025, and about 88.7 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. The typical owned home is valued around $669,900, so even a small change in an exemption or assessment moves real money. If you are unsure which office to call first, call the receiver for amounts owed and the assessor for anything about value or exemptions.

Due dates and penalties

The tax year begins December 1 and ends November 30. One bill is mailed around mid-December. You can pay it all at once or in two halves, and there is no grace period on either date.

Ways to pay a Smithtown tax bill

The Receiver of Taxes works from 99 W. Main Street. The payment window closes at 4:30 p.m., and summer hours end earlier, at 4 p.m. Your choices:

  • Online, by credit card or e-check, with a service fee added.
  • By phone through the automated line posted on the town page, also with a fee.

If you mail a check, send it early enough that the postmark lands before the due date, and write the district, section, block and lot so it is credited to the right parcel.

How assessment works and how to appeal

The Department of Assessment sets each property's fair market value. If the figure looks like what a sale would bring, you do nothing. If it looks too high, you use the grievance process. Grievance Day falls on the third Tuesday of May.

Exemptions run on a separate clock. Applications must reach the department by 5:00 p.m. on March 1. A STAR application only needs a postmark of that day, and when March 1 lands on a weekend the deadline moves to Monday. An approved exemption shows on the next December bill. Denial letters are mailed by May 1, which leaves time to grieve before Grievance Day.

A reduction won through a small claims petition normally appears on the tax bill. If it arrives late in the year, the second half may be adjusted, and if that is too late Suffolk County refunds the owner directly. The assessor's office is at (631) 360-7560.

When a bill goes up, the usual reasons are:

  • A higher rate set by a taxing district.
  • A higher assessed value.
  • An exemption that lapsed or was never renewed.
  • A new owner who does not qualify for the seller's exemption.

Because a lapsed exemption is one reason bills climb, confirm yours is current before you pick a closing date.

Before you sell a Smithtown house

Start with the receiver. Ask for the amount currently due on your parcel, since neither half has a grace period and unpaid balances after May 31 move to Suffolk County. The tax map number appears on the bill, and the receiver asks for the district, section, block and lot on any mailed check.

Next, visit the Building Department at 23 Redwood Lane. It enforces the State building code and the town's zoning, issues permits and certificates of occupancy, and searches its records at no charge to see whether each permit has a matching certificate. Work done without a permit will not have one. A home built before permits began in 1947 can request a History Letter. Duplicate certificates with a raised seal are sold for a fee, and inspections are booked at (631) 360-7522. The department takes no applications inside the Village of the Branch, Nissequogue or Head of the Harbor.

These projects need a permit, so look back over what you have added to the house:

  • Pools able to hold water deeper than 24 inches, with a 4 to 6 foot fence or self-latching gate.
  • Fences over four feet tall.
  • Detached sheds over 144 square feet and 12 feet tall, and other accessory structures over 50 square feet.
  • A wider window opening or changed header, and any skylight.
  • New gables or a changed roof pitch, though not simple re-shingling.
  • Decks more than 8 inches above grade.

Deeds, transfer tax and a quick sale

Deeds are filed with the Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead. The state's base transfer tax is the seller's to pay unless the contract says otherwise. Your closing attorney or title company usually carries the paperwork and pulls the tax payoff from the receiver or, after May 31, from the County Comptroller.

A sale to a cash buyer skips the mortgage appraisal and lender conditions, but it does not skip taxes or permits. Open permits, missing certificates of occupancy and unpaid balances still have to be cleared, so gather the permit history and the current bill before you accept an offer.

A simple order of work helps. First, request the amount due from the receiver and confirm which half is paid. Second, ask the Building Department to compare your permits with your certificates of occupancy, and fix any gap early. Third, check with the Department of Assessment that your exemption is still on the roll, and tell the buyer if it will end at sale. Fourth, hand the title company the bill, the district name and the tax map number. Doing these before listing keeps surprises out of the final week before closing. Several districts straddle town lines, so read the district name printed on your bill and give it to the title company.

By January 10, without penalty. The bill goes out once a year in mid-December, and there is no grace period.

To Suffolk County. The Receiver of Taxes cannot take payments postmarked after May 31.

What is the smallest partial payment Smithtown takes?

$200. Penalties apply only to the balance left after the due date.

When is Grievance Day in Smithtown?

The third Tuesday of May. Exemption denials are mailed by May 1, which leaves time to file.

The Department of Assessment must have the application by 5:00 p.m. on March 1, though STAR applications may be postmarked that day. A weekend date moves the deadline to Monday.

Which office sends the Southampton tax bill?

The Town of Southampton Receiver of Taxes bills and collects from December 1 through May 31, and the Suffolk County Comptroller takes over after that. The Receiver's office sits on the main floor of Town Hall at 116 Hampton Road, phone 631-702-2470, with weekday counter hours of 8:30 a.m. through 4:00 p.m. The Assessor, who sets the value your bill is built on, works from the same address and answers at 631-283-6020.

The town includes seven incorporated villages (North Haven, Quogue, Sag Harbor, Sagaponack, Southampton, Westhampton Beach and West Hampton Dunes) and 16 hamlets, among them Hampton Bays, Bridgehampton, Flanders and Shinnecock Hills. If you are unsure which bill covers your address, call the Receiver before you sign a contract.

  • Receiver of Taxes: bills, receipts, duplicate bills, address changes, first-half and second-half payments.
  • Assessor: values, exemption applications, grievance forms, the tentative roll.
  • County Comptroller: every unpaid balance after May 31, plus tax liens.

Due dates for the 2026-27 bill

The first half is owed by January 10, 2027. Because that is a Sunday, the Town moves the deadline to Monday, January 11. The second half is owed by May 31, 2027. Bills go out by December 15, but the Receiver cannot mail them or take money until the Suffolk County Legislature approves the tax warrant, which usually comes after the lien date of December 1, 2026.

A bill that never shows up does not extend the penalty-free period. New York law holds the owner responsible either way, and the Town's online portal can print a duplicate. Mailed payments count by the USPS postmark on the envelope. A private metered postmark does not count, so send certified mail if you are near a deadline.

What late payment costs

First-half tax paid after January 10 still goes to the Receiver, with 1 percent interest added to the base amount for each month. Anything unpaid after May 31 draws a 5 percent penalty and 5 percent interest, and the Town can no longer take those payments. They go to the County Comptroller, who adds a further 1 percent a month until the balance is cleared.

Partial payments are possible. The Receiver takes installments of at least $200 under Suffolk County Resolution 551-2001, and interest then runs only on the unpaid balance. The Comptroller also accepts partial payments on delinquent tax. The county phone for balance questions is 631-852-3000, and the Comptroller's mailing address is 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901.

  • Online: $1.75 for an ACH payment, or a 2.5 percent fee by credit card, charged by the processor and not by the Town.

  • A check or ACH payment returned by your bank for any reason cancels the tax payment, so the tax is treated as unpaid.

Looking up your bill and changing the mailing address

Use the Town's eTax portal. The easiest search is by street address, but you can also search by owner last name, tax map number or the current bill number, and no username or password is required. The record shows the owner, tax map number, zoning and taxes due. For help with the portal, the Citizens' Response Center answers at 631-702-2440 on weekdays, 8:30 a.m. until the 4 p.m. close.

A missing bill usually means the Town has an old mailing address. Send a change-of-address form to 116 Hampton Road, Southampton, NY 11968, fax it to 631-287-5732 or drop a copy at Town Hall. The portal's Duplicate Tax Bill option prints a fresh copy at once. Suffolk County also advises owners to tell the Assessor about any new mailing address so the roll is corrected before bills go out in December.

Before you list, pull the bill for the current year and check the Property Location box in the upper left corner. It carries the official street address and house number, and your buyer's title company will compare it with the deed and survey.

How to challenge your assessment or claim an exemption

File a grievance by Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in May, which is May 18 in 2027. The Assessor's Office at Town Hall helps with the application the week before, and appointments go through 631-283-6020. The tentative roll appears around May 1, so review it first. The town review board decides complaints, and it meets off and on from June through September to work through filings.

The Town's grievance page gives the state equalization rate and residential assessment ratio for Southampton as 59.7 percent. Use that ratio when you set your assessed value beside a sale price or appraisal.

Exemptions need an application at the Assessor by March 1. Programs the Town lists:

  • STAR and Enhanced STAR for primary residences.
  • Senior citizens.
  • Military service.
  • Persons with disabilities and limited incomes.
  • First-time homebuyers.
  • Volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers.

A buyer does not inherit a seller's military-service or senior exemption, so the bill can rise sharply after a sale. Tell your buyer this early so the monthly cost is no surprise.

Selling with taxes owed

Unpaid tax stays attached to the property, so it has to be settled at or before closing. Your closing attorney or title company will request a tax payoff from the Receiver before May 31, or from the County Comptroller after it. Send them the full tax-bill description of the parcel, since the Comptroller asks for it on every inquiry.

Suffolk's collection path is slower than many people expect. After May 31 the County sells a tax lien to itself, usually in the autumn or December. A one-, two- or three-family home can be redeemed within 36 months of the lien sale, other property within 12, and after that the County issues a tax deed. The Town's FAQ says the Treasurer typically starts collection on vacant land after one year and on improved property after three years of non-payment. Redemption after a deed is handled by the Suffolk Department of Planning, Division of Real Estate, at 631-853-5900.

If you paid off a mortgage during the tax year, check with the Receiver whether the bank already paid the full year. The bank will not necessarily forward that information, and the owner stays liable for late-payment penalties.

Southampton homes carry high values. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $928,100, about 82.4 percent are lived in by their owners, and median gross rent is $2,363. The 2025 population estimate is 71,601, up from 69,036 in the 2020 census.

With values at that level, a tax bill that jumps after a sale matters to a buyer. Before you list, gather the current bill, any exemption letters, and the Receiver's payoff figure. Hand them to your attorney so a cash buyer or a financed buyer can see the full carrying cost without waiting on the Town.

Buyers of waterfront and low-lying properties often ask about drainage and flood history, so collect those records too.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay Southampton property tax in person?

At the Receiver of Taxes on the main floor of Town Hall, 116 Hampton Road, weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Cash, checks and money orders are accepted, and you can also pay online or by mail.

Can I pay Southampton property tax in two parts?

Yes. One half is owed by January 10 (January 11 in 2027) and the other half by May 31. Smaller partial payments of at least $200 are also accepted, with interest charged only on the remaining balance.

What happens if I miss the May 31 deadline in Southampton?

Payment moves to the Suffolk County Comptroller, and the balance picks up a 5 percent penalty plus interest. The Town can no longer take your payment after that date.

When is the Southampton exemption deadline?

March 1 for new or renewed exemptions, filed with the Assessor at 116 Hampton Road. Call 631-283-6020 to ask which application fits your situation.

Do I still owe tax if my Southampton bill never arrived?

Yes. Under New York law the owner is responsible for the tax whether or not a bill arrives. Ask the Receiver for a duplicate or print one from the Town's tax portal.

Who bills and collects property tax in Syracuse

One office, the City Payment Center, prepares the bill and takes payment for City, School and County property tax together. The Department of Assessment sets the value. Due dates and address changes

Due dates are printed on your bill. If you need them for the current year, call the City Payment Center at 315-448-8310. The same office can tell you what you owe today and whether any prior year is open. A tax question that reaches the Assessment office gets routed to the Payment Center anyway.

If bills are going to the wrong place, file a Change of Address for City Service Notifications with the Department of Assessment. The form covers tax bills, assessment notices and other property mail. Owners who have moved away or inherited a house should file it before the next bill cycle.

Homeowners who have fallen behind can apply for a tax trust, the City's payment plan for delinquent property tax. The application is a PDF on the Payment Center page. Parcels that go through tax foreclosure are transferred to the Greater Syracuse Property Development Corporation, known as the Land Bank, and are then offered for sale there.

When you visit the Payment Center, bring your bill or the parcel address, and any letter you received about a past-due balance. Ask for a printout of what is owed and what has been paid, so you can hand it to your closing attorney. If you are applying for a tax trust, ask what the first payment must be before you leave.

How to challenge your Syracuse assessment

File a formal grievance with the Board of Assessment Review during the last two weeks of January. The board has four or five officers appointed by the City Council, and it can lower an assessment for good cause. Grounds include an assessment that is unequal, excessive or unlawful, and a wrong property classification.

Fill out the grievance form, print it and sign it by hand. Bring or mail it to City Hall, Suite 130. The office takes only forms with an original signature, complete documentation, and a filing date inside those two weeks. Forms that arrive early or late are not taken. Evening and Saturday-morning hours have been posted during the window.

State law requires every property to be held at a uniform percentage of market value (RPTL sections 301 and 305). Syracuse values by cost, income and comparable sales, then adjusts for physical changes or market shifts. Each parcel has its own market value, which is why neighbors' assessments differ. Gather recent sales of similar houses before you file.

Syracuse housing numbers

Syracuse is a city of renters. The owner-occupancy rate for 2020-2024 is 41.6 percent, the median owner-occupied value is $138,400 and median gross rent is $1,039. Median household income is $47,819. The 2020 census counted 148,620 people, and the July 2025 estimate is 144,896.

With values at that level, a tax bill that is high for the neighborhood can weigh on a sale. If you think your assessment is out of line, the January grievance window is the time to act, and a listing in the spring means you may already have missed it.

Where do I pay my Syracuse property tax?

At the City Payment Center, Room 122 in City Hall, 233 East Washington Street, Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. It collects City, School and County tax in one place.

Does the STAR credit lower a Syracuse bill directly?

Only for owners registered before 2015. Newer registrants get a credit check or direct deposit from New York State, which they use to pay City and School tax.

It is transferred to the Greater Syracuse Property Development Corporation, the Land Bank, which lists available properties for sale.

If you cannot find a tax return or proof of income, the Assessor's Office can advise on the non-filer worksheets the Town provides for senior and disabled applicants. Call 716-877-8811 to ask which form fits you.

You qualify only if you own and live in a one-, two- or three-family home, filed a timely complaint with the Board and ask for no bigger reduction than you sought there. Who bills property tax in White Plains

The City of White Plains Finance Department bills and collects at City Hall, 255 Main Street, Room 102. The City Assessor sets the values the bill is based on. White Plains is the seat of Westchester County, and one household can receive a city and school bill in July and January, and a county bill in April.

Bills are made out to the owner of record. Under RPTL 922, a bill that never reaches the owner does not cancel the tax or stop penalties and interest from running. If one fails to arrive, call 914-422-1248 so the address can be verified and a duplicate mailed.

Due dates and interest

Taxes come due three times a year: July 1 and January 1 for city and school tax, and April 1 for county tax. The city allows payment through the last day of each month without interest, so the practical deadlines are July 31, January 31 and April 30.

Bills are mailed in mid-December, late March and June. Payments must be postmarked or hand-delivered by the due date, or they carry interest. Overdue tax and water charges accrue interest at 1 percent a month, and state law gives the city no power to waive that interest for any reason.

Ways to pay a White Plains bill

You can pay in person, online, by mail or by automatic debit. City Hall accepts payments from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on days other than holidays, at the Finance Department window in Room 102.

  • Mail with the stub: make the check out to the Commissioner of Finance and send it to P.O. Box 5086, White Plains, NY 10602-5086.

  • Online: the city runs a portal for tax and water payments by credit card.

Ownership changes are recorded by the Assessor, who needs a certified copy of the recorded deed. A change of mailing address for billing goes in on the Tax Account Change Form. Owners can also name a consenting third party to receive copies of bills, using the Third Party Notification Form.

How to challenge a White Plains assessment

File a complaint on form RP-524 between January 1 and January 21 with the Assessor or the Board of Assessment Review. The Board meets on January 21 under the City Charter. On Thursday, January 21, 2027 it sits by appointment from 3 to 5 p.m. and 7 to 9 p.m. in the Common Council Chambers, Room 203, at City Hall. Call 914-422-1223 to book a time.

White Plains runs on a different calendar from towns that hold a May grievance day. The taxable status date is December 1, the tentative roll is January 1, the final roll is March 1, and exemptions are processed from April 1 through December 1. A late complaint loses the right to review, so mark January on the calendar before you list.

Bring evidence of market value, such as recent sales of comparable homes nearby or an appraisal. The Board decides whether an assessment is unequal, excessive or in the wrong class.

How a White Plains tax bill is figured

Two things set it: the property's taxable assessment and the levies of the jurisdictions that tax it. The tax rate is the levy divided by the total taxable assessed value, and the assessment reflects the property's value less any exemptions the owner qualifies for.

That is why an exemption can change a bill without touching the city's budget. The Assessor processes exemption applications from April 1 through December 1 each year. Ask the Assessor which exemptions are on your parcel before you give a buyer a bill to rely on.

Water charges when you sell

Unpaid water charges do not disappear. They are relevied against the property as a tax lien on the following July 1. A seller with an old water balance can therefore find it folded into the next tax bill and into the payoff.

Residential water in the city is divided into six districts, each billed twice a year, and a final water reading costs $75 when requested by calling 914-422-1211. Schedule the reading with the closing so the water account closes cleanly and the buyer starts with a clear record. If the property has water service, an available-on-demand charge based on meter size is billed even when no water is used.

White Plains housing numbers

The city had 62,871 residents in July 2025. Owners hold 51.0 percent of homes, so renters are nearly half of households, and the 2020 to 2024 median value of an owner-occupied home is $620,800. Median monthly owner costs run $3,525 with a mortgage and $1,494 without one, and median gross rent is $2,269.

The city covers only 9.74 square miles of land, so a sale price on the next street over is often a better guide than any citywide median.

Selling a White Plains house with tax due

Ask the Finance Department for a payoff that includes city, school, county and any water relevy, and confirm the date to which interest is calculated. A few steps keep the sale clean.

  • Check which of the July, January and April installments are paid.
  • Ask whether any water charges were relevied on a July 1 bill.
  • Make sure the Assessor has the current deed and owner name on file.
  • If you plan to contest the value, file by January 21, since a late complaint loses the right to review.

A cash buyer can close with open tax, and the title company pays the balance from the proceeds. Since interest is 1 percent each month, a closing date that slips past month end changes the number.

Frequently asked questions

When are White Plains property taxes due?

City and school tax is due July 1 and January 1, and county tax is due April 1. The city accepts payment through the last day of each of those months, and interest applies after that.

What is the White Plains late interest rate?

It is 1 percent a month on overdue taxes and water charges. State law prevents the Finance Department from waiving interest or penalties on a late payment.

When is White Plains grievance day?

There is no May grievance day. Complaints are filed January 1 through January 21 with the Assessor or the Board of Assessment Review, which meets on January 21 by appointment. Call 914-422-1223.

Can I set up automatic payments for White Plains taxes?

Yes. Sign and return the city's authorization agreement to the Finance Department at 255 Main Street, Room 102. The city then debits your checking or savings account on each due date.

How do I change the owner name on a White Plains tax bill?

Only the Assessor's Office can record a change of ownership, and it needs a certified copy of the recorded deed. A change of mailing address goes through the Tax Account Change Form.

How many property tax bills a Yonkers homeowner gets

Two a year. The City of Yonkers sends one in March for Westchester County tax and one in July for city and school tax. The county bill is paid once, usually in April. The city and school bill is split into three equal installments, with three stubs at the bottom.

The Tax Office sits in City Hall at 40 South Broadway. The Assessment Department in the same building sets the values that the bills are built on. The city offers an online property tax portal where any parcel can be researched for free.

  • Tax Office, City Hall Room 108: payments, bill copies and payment history. The owner can call 914-377-6138, 914-377-6141 or 914-377-6146.
  • Assessment Department, City Hall, phone 914-377-6200: parcel updates, exemptions and assessment appeals.
  • Cashier's Office, first floor of City Hall, Room 108: in-person payments.

Installment due dates

The first city and school installment date moves each year, because it is set 30 days after the City Council adopts the budget, usually in June. The second is always October 6 and the third is always January 6, shifted off a weekend. The next one on the calendar is Wednesday, January 6, 2027.

Yonkers tax installment schedule
BillInstallmentDue
City and schoolFirst30 days after the Council adopts the budget
City and schoolSecondOctober 6
City and schoolThirdJanuary 6 (Wednesday, January 6, 2027)
Westchester CountySingle payment30 days after the county adopts its budget, usually April

The county bill is adopted around March and falls due 30 days later, so the date each year depends on when the county passes its budget.

Late payment in Yonkers

Interest starts immediately, because the Tax Office allows no grace period on an installment. The rate is 15 percent a year, simple interest, calculated daily from the confirmation date through the day of payment. The city cannot waive that interest for any reason.

The office decides whether a payment arrived on time by the postmark on the envelope. Local banks no longer accept Yonkers tax payments, so mail goes to City of Yonkers, 40 South Broadway, Room 108, Yonkers, NY 10701. Online payment by credit card or electronic check is also available, and Yonkers.MunicipalTaxPayments.com shows outstanding taxes.

If you receive a delinquent notice for a bill you already paid, mail a copy of the front and back of the check and any receipt to the Tax Office at City Hall. Owners who get a delinquent tax letter should review the parcel in the online portal for details.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to challenge a Yonkers assessment

File a complaint with the Board of Assessment Review between November 1 and November 15. Yonkers uses a fall calendar rather than a May grievance day. The valuation date is July 1, the taxable status date is October 15 and the tentative roll comes out November 1.

  • November 1 to 15: grievance period for complaints to the Board.
  • December 15: deadline to send additional information or ask for a personal hearing.
  • Last Monday in January through the third Friday in February: personal hearings.
  • April 10 to May 10: window to file Small Claims Assessment Review or certiorari, open only to owners who already filed a protest with the Board.

The final roll is published on April 10. If this year's window is closed, the next one opens November 1, 2027. An owner who plans to sell can mention a pending protest to the buyer.

Exemption filing deadline

Applications are due by October 15 each year. That covers senior citizen, disability and military-service exemption filings and renewals, and the date moves to the next business day when it lands on a weekend or holiday. The Assessment Department asks owners to apply by September 15 if they can.

An exemption stays on the roll only if it is renewed, so a seller who has had one for years should confirm the renewal is current. Ask the Assessment Department at 914-377-6200 what is on file for your parcel.

What title companies need from the Yonkers Tax Office

Title companies can research a parcel online for free, or they can pay a $5 fee per property per year for the Tax Department to do it. Title and mortgage companies are encouraged to use the city's online property portal and the municipal tax payment site first. Without a processed fee the office gives no information by phone or email, and it asks for two to three weeks of lead time.

Make checks for that fee payable to the City of Yonkers at 40 South Broadway, Room 108. If you are the seller, order the payoff early. Owners can also ask the Tax Office for copies of prior or current bills and for a history of payments.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Yonkers housing numbers

Yonkers had an estimated 212,603 residents in July 2025, across 81,645 households. Only 46.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so renters hold a majority, and the median value of an owner-occupied home was $501,600 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $1,784, and owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $3,028.

A citywide median hides neighborhood differences, so check recent sales on your own block before you set a price.

Selling a Yonkers house with tax due

Start with the online parcel record, then confirm the exact figure with the Tax Office. Because installments carry no grace period, the date matters.

  • List which of the July, October and January installments are paid, and whether the April county bill is paid.
  • Ask for the interest through the planned closing date at 15 percent a year.
  • Check the exemption renewal date on October 15.
  • Find out whether a Board of Assessment Review complaint or a small claims case is pending.

A cash buyer does not need the taxes cleared first. The title company pays the open balances out of your proceeds at closing, and the Yonkers Tax Office can supply the payoff.

In practice the order is simple. Look up the parcel in the portal, call or visit the Tax Office with the address, request the payoff through the planned closing date, and send that figure to your attorney or title company. If a closing moves, ask for a fresh figure, since interest is calculated daily. Bring copies of bills or payment history if the portal and your own records disagree, and ask the office to correct anything before the buyer's title search turns it up.

Frequently asked questions

When is the next Yonkers property tax installment due?

The third city and school installment is due Wednesday, January 6, 2027. The county bill is usually adopted in March and due 30 days later.

How much is the late interest on Yonkers property tax?

It is 15 percent a year, simple interest, calculated daily from the confirmation date. There is no grace period, and the city cannot waive the interest for any reason.

When can I file a Yonkers assessment complaint?

From November 1 to November 15 with the Board of Assessment Review. Supporting documents and personal hearing requests are due by December 15, and hearings begin on the last Monday in January.

Where do I pay Yonkers taxes in person?

At the Cashier's Office on the first floor of City Hall, 40 South Broadway, Room 108. You can also mail a check to the same address or pay online by credit card or electronic check.

How can a title company get Yonkers tax information?

Title companies can use the online property portal and the municipal tax payment site for free. A $5 fee per property per year applies if the Tax Department does the research, with two to three weeks of lead time.
